    kind=exploratory + related_to  -> edge drawn
    kind=choice      + related_to  -> written, NO edge, reply silent

THE CAUSE — two changes, each right alone:
  · chg:the-relatedness-judgement-rides-the-refusal (#394, 2026-08-30) added `related_to` and processes it only inside `if exploratory && (related_to || no_relation_note)`. Its scoping was about the DEMAND ("a choice is not asked"), and its only test on the boundary asserts exactly that (a_choice_is_not_asked_even_when_it_has_near_matches). No test covers a choice that VOLUNTEERS relations; dropping them was a side effect, not a decision.
  · chg:four-root-causes-from-two-field-reports-are-fixed-at-the-cause (#527, 2026-09-17), "the guard reads the request": `declared_targets` exempts from the near-match refusal any id named in `satisfies`, `allocated_to` or `related_to`, because "the request has already said how the two relate". True for the first two, which are always drawn; false for `related_to` outside the exploratory branch.
  ⇒ On a choice, `related_to` does the guard's work and none of its own: the near-duplicate the guard exists to stop lands UNLINKED to what it resembles.

⑥ THE CLASS: a guard or reader that treats an argument as done (the exemption) where the executor only acts on it conditionally — an invariant ("every declared target is an edge after the call") that nothing states or checks. And the reply echoes the node, not the relations, so the drop is invisible — the unreadable-success shape.

WHAT WOULD FIX THE CLASS, not built: draw offered `related_to` for every kind (the demand stays exploratory-only, which is what #394 meant); echo the relations drawn in the reply; and pin the invariant with a test that fails today — for every kind, each id that exempted the guard is an edge after the call.
